newsitem.title: UK: Kleinwort Benson to restructure UK equity trading.
newsitem.headline: Kleinwort Benson to restructure UK equity trading.

text.p: Kleinwort Benson will on Monday rejig its UK equity trading activities, becoming the latest brokerage to reorganise in preparation for far-reaching reforms of the London stock market which take effect next year.

Kleinwort said it would split its 20-strong UK equity market-making team into two groups, covering stocks in the blue chip FTSE 100 index and second-line shares, and replacing the current system where stocks are traded according to sector.

The move comes after Merrill Lynch earlier this month said it would adopt a similar structure in preparation for the move next year to so-called "order-driven" trading, where trades will be matched by computer rather than by dealers in broking houses.

"We are regrouping to cover the FTSE 100 and mid-cap separately," said Martin Lupton, head of equity trading at Kleinwort. "Next year the way the market is going to be run will change and we want to gain experience ahead of that."
Under plans laid out by the London Stock Exchange (LSE), the role of the large teams of market-makers employed by London brokerage will change significantly.

Brokers will match trades on the LSE's new Sequence 6 computer system but will also be able to trade large blocks of stock off screen -- although the new order-driven regime will initially apply just to FTSE 100 shares.
Other brokerages such as UBS have also regrouped their share trading operations to pave the way for next year's reforms.
